content_html:
UV5-RM-MOD

This repo contains new firmware for Baofeng UV5-RM radios adding new apps including texting. CAUTION: CHIRP will no longer work so use the included apps to program channels and categories

Custom firmware and add-on apps for the Baofeng UV-5RM, built on the open-source bf-5rh-firmware-open. The main addition is TEXT: short text messages between two radios, with delivery confirmation and no phone, internet or extra hardware.

Flashing can't be undone. No copy of the factory firmware is known for this hardware, so there's no way back to stock, and CHIRP stops working with the radio. A bad flash could brick it. This has only been run on two radios, so use it at your own risk.

What it adds

Feature What it does
TEXT Sends messages up to 50 characters, retries until confirmed, saves them, and plays a tone when one arrives
Scan modes Press Band to switch between Weather, Police/Fire/EMS, Air, Repeaters, FRS, GMRS, MURS and more, or type a custom range
BAND SWEEP Sweeps a whole band for activity
RPT FINDER Works out a repeater's input frequency and tone
FOX HUNT Signal meter and rough distance estimate for finding a transmitter
SEARCH/QT SCAN Finds a nearby signal's frequency, or the tone on your channel; press 1 to switch
Look and feel Skull start-up logo, black and red menus, and a custom start-up tune

Screenshots: see the preview_*.png files in UV-5RM Custom Firmware.

Before you start: check your radio

This firmware only fits one hardware version. Radios that look identical can have a different chip.

  1. Turn the radio off, then hold 8 while turning it on.
  2. Read the text on the screen, then turn the radio off without pressing anything else.
Screen says What to do
5RHNRFB-YP07 This is the right hardware, so carry on
Anything else, such as ...NRF or ...BK Don't flash it. It may boot but not transmit or receive

What you need

  • A Windows PC. The tools are Python, so other systems may work, but they're untested.
  • Python, plus the serial library: py -m pip install pyserial
  • A Baofeng programming cable. The commands below assume COM3, so change it to match your port.

Run these from the UV-5RM Custom Firmware folder.

Install

1. Back up the radio. Flash mode can't read it, so do this first, with the radio on and on its main screen. This only reads. It may not answer until the radio has been power-cycled, and the folder has to exist.

mkdir my-backup
py source-changes\radio_read.py COM3 my-backup\factory_memory.img

2. Enter flash mode. Turn the radio off, hold both side buttons and turn it on. The screen stays black. Check that it answers (this doesn't write anything):

py source-changes\bootloader_probe.py COM3

3. Flash. This is the point of no return. It takes under a minute, so don't touch the radio or the cable. The long number is a checksum, and the tool refuses a file that doesn't match it.

py source-changes\flash_bf.py UV-5RM_Custom_Firmware.BF COM3 4340f205430f0741

4. Install the logo and apps. Wait for the radio to restart to its main screen. This reads everything back to confirm it.

py source-changes\setup_radio.py COM3 skull_logo.rgb565 64 apps

5. Turn on transmit. It starts off as a safety step. Go to SETTINGS and set TXINH to off.

6. Load channels (optional). Open UV-5RM_Channel_Uploader.html in Chrome or Edge. The channel list in this repo is for Clark County, Nevada, so check that it suits your area. Your radio should keep whatever channels it already had.

To choose which channels get scanned, open UV-5RM_Scan_Builder.html, tick the ones you want, and load the CSV it saves into the uploader.

Optional extras: set_boot_tune.py sets a Doom-style start-up riff, and set_radio2_mario_tune.py sets a Super Mario one but only runs on one specific radio, so copy and edit it for yours.

Using TEXT

Both radios need TEXT open, on the same simplex frequency. It uses the frequency the radio was on when you opened it. Don't use a repeater.

Key Action
Number keys Type, flip-phone style; the letters are shown at the top of the screen
Menu Send
Exit Delete a letter; stops retries while sending; closes the app when nothing is typed
Hold Exit Close the app
Up / Down Scroll saved messages
* Send a numbered test ping
A/B Switch between low (default) and high power
Hold # twice Erase all saved messages
Mark Meaning
> Sent, waiting for a reply
+ The other radio confirmed it
! Never confirmed. It may still have arrived, since only the reply may have been lost
< Received

Limits:

  • A radio only receives while TEXT is open.
  • It's built for two radios; with more, the automatic replies would collide.
  • Messages have no encryption, and they're stored unencrypted on the radio. Scrambling isn't security, so any radio with this app can read them.
  • Range and long messages have barely been tested. Most testing was short pings a few feet apart.

Legal

You're responsible for what you transmit.

  • TEXT transmits on its own. With the app open, the radio sends a reply automatically to any message it receives, so stay on a frequency you're licensed for.
  • Ham bands: you need a license and must identify with your callsign. TEXT doesn't send one, so you'd have to identify by voice. Encrypting messages isn't allowed.
  • FRS, GMRS and MURS: this radio isn't type-accepted for them, so treat those channels as receive-only. Rules also vary by country.
  • Power: output hasn't been measured, and the radio's actual power may differ from its label.

Building from source

firmware-source is the complete source of the provided firmware and apps; the firmware and TEXT were confirmed to rebuild byte for byte. It needs Rust and the target in its rust-toolchain.toml. Use a short --target-dir, because long paths break linking on Windows.

cargo build --release --manifest-path firmware-source/Cargo.toml --config firmware-source/.cargo/config.toml --target-dir C:/t/fw
py source-changes/elf2bin.py C:/t/fw/thumbv7em-none-eabi/release/bf5rh-fw fw.bin

source-changes holds the patches against upstream and the PC tools. source-changes/simulator runs the apps against a simulated radio, with no hardware needed:

cargo build --release --manifest-path source-changes/simulator/Cargo.toml --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --target-dir C:/t/sim
C:/t/sim/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/release/sim.exe out-folder skull_logo.rgb565

The output folder has to exist. The simulator only checks logic, so it can't prove how a real radio behaves on the air.

Credits and license

  • Firmware base: bf-5rh-firmware-open
  • Modem settings researched from the UV-K5 community's messenger firmware
  • Licensed under GPL-3.0, the same as the firmware it's built on. See LICENSE.

Provided as is, with no warranty.

This repo contains new firmware for Baofeng UV5-RM radios adding new apps including texting. CAUTION: CHIRP will no longer work so use the included apps to program channels and categories

Custom firmware and add-on apps for the Baofeng UV-5RM, built on the open-source bf-5rh-firmware-open. The main addition is TEXT: short text messages between two radios, with delivery confirmation and no phone, internet or extra hardware.

Flashing can't be undone. No copy of the factory firmware is known for this hardware, so there's no way back to stock, and CHIRP stops working with the radio. A bad flash could brick it. This has only been run on two radios, so use it at your own risk.

Before you start: check your radio

This firmware only fits one hardware version. Radios that look identical can have a different chip.

  1. Turn the radio off, then hold 8 while turning it on.
  2. Read the text on the screen, then turn the radio off without pressing anything else.
Screen says 该怎么办
5RHNRFB-YP07 This is the right hardware, so carry on
Anything else, such as ...NRF or ...BK Don't flash it. It may boot but not transmit or receive

你需要什么

  • A Windows PC. The tools are Python, so other systems may work, but they're untested.
  • Python, plus the serial library: py -m pip install pyserial
  • A Baofeng programming cable. The commands below assume COM3, so change it to match your port.

Run these from the UV-5RM Custom Firmware folder.

安装

1. Back up the radio. Flash mode can't read it, so do this first, with the radio on and on its main screen. This only reads. It may not answer until the radio has been power-cycled, and the folder has to exist.

mkdir my-backup
py source-changes\radio_read.py COM3 my-backup\factory_memory.img

2. Enter flash mode. Turn the radio off, hold both side buttons and turn it on. The screen stays black. Check that it answers (this doesn't write anything):

py source-changes\bootloader_probe.py COM3

3. Flash. This is the point of no return. It takes under a minute, so don't touch the radio or the cable. The long number is a checksum, and the tool refuses a file that doesn't match it.

py source-changes\flash_bf.py UV-5RM_Custom_Firmware.BF COM3 4340f205430f0741

4. Install the logo and apps. Wait for the radio to restart to its main screen. This reads everything back to confirm it.

py source-changes\setup_radio.py COM3 skull_logo.rgb565 64 apps

5. Turn on transmit. It starts off as a safety step. Go to SETTINGS and set TXINH to off.

6. Load channels (optional). Open UV-5RM_Channel_Uploader.html in Chrome or Edge. The channel list in this repo is for Clark County, Nevada, so check that it suits your area. Your radio should keep whatever channels it already had.

To choose which channels get scanned, open UV-5RM_Scan_Builder.html, tick the ones you want, and load the CSV it saves into the uploader.

Optional extras: set_boot_tune.py sets a Doom-style start-up riff, and set_radio2_mario_tune.py sets a Super Mario one but only runs on one specific radio, so copy and edit it for yours.

Using TEXT

Both radios need TEXT open, on the same simplex frequency. It uses the frequency the radio was on when you opened it. Don't use a repeater.

Key 行动
Number keys Type, flip-phone style; the letters are shown at the top of the screen
Menu Send
Exit Delete a letter; stops retries while sending; closes the app when nothing is typed
Hold Exit Close the app
Up / Down Scroll saved messages
* Send a numbered test ping
A/B Switch between low (default) and high power
Hold # twice Erase all saved messages
Mark 意义
> Sent, waiting for a reply
+ The other radio confirmed it
! Never confirmed. It may still have arrived, since only the reply may have been lost
< Received

Limits:

  • A radio only receives while TEXT is open.
  • It's built for two radios; with more, the automatic replies would collide.
  • Messages have no encryption, and they're stored unencrypted on the radio. Scrambling isn't security, so any radio with this app can read them.
  • Range and long messages have barely been tested. Most testing was short pings a few feet apart.

Legal

You're responsible for what you transmit.

  • TEXT transmits on its own. With the app open, the radio sends a reply automatically to any message it receives, so stay on a frequency you're licensed for.
  • Ham bands: you need a license and must identify with your callsign. TEXT doesn't send one, so you'd have to identify by voice. Encrypting messages isn't allowed.
  • FRS, GMRS and MURS: this radio isn't type-accepted for them, so treat those channels as receive-only. Rules also vary by country.
  • Power: output hasn't been measured, and the radio's actual power may differ from its label.

从源头构建

firmware-source is the complete source of the provided firmware and apps; the firmware and TEXT were confirmed to rebuild byte for byte. It needs Rust and the target in its rust-toolchain.toml. Use a short --target-dir, because long paths break linking on Windows.

cargo build --release --manifest-path firmware-source/Cargo.toml --config firmware-source/.cargo/config.toml --target-dir C:/t/fw
py source-changes/elf2bin.py C:/t/fw/thumbv7em-none-eabi/release/bf5rh-fw fw.bin

source-changes holds the patches against upstream and the PC tools. source-changes/simulator runs the apps against a simulated radio, with no hardware needed:

cargo build --release --manifest-path source-changes/simulator/Cargo.toml --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --target-dir C:/t/sim
C:/t/sim/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/release/sim.exe out-folder skull_logo.rgb565

The output folder has to exist. The simulator only checks logic, so it can't prove how a real radio behaves on the air.
